paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the last bar, the lighter bar is 46.73%, and the darker bar is 0.11%, which is negligible in the image). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning reduces biases to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across community and healthcare when tuned on education and workplace scenario prompts.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the percentage of biased responses generated before and after instruction tuning for three categories: Sports, Community, and Healthcare. The horizontal axis represents the categories, listed alphabetically, while the vertical axis represents “Bias Percentage” on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 70, with tick marks at 10-unit intervals. Each category features three stacked bars, representing “No Contact Before”, “Positive Contact Before”, and “Negative Contact Before” in light gray, red, and light blue respectively, as well as “No Contact After”, “Positive Contact After”, and “Negative Contact After” in dark gray, dark red, and dark blue respectively. For Sports, the “No Contact Before” bar is approximately 45.42%, with “Positive Contact Before” at 43.65% and “Negative Contact Before” at 50.05%; the corresponding “After” bars reach 7.45%, 8.31%, and 8.33% respectively. For Community, the “Before” bars are 38.08%, 35.38%, and 40.79%, while the “After” bars are 0.00%, 0.01%, and 0.00% respectively. Healthcare shows “Before” bars of 40.70%, 37.51%, and 46.73%, and “After” bars of 0.00%, 0.01%, and 0.11% respectively. The bars are not visually emphasized with any shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
